summary: Paul Williams worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Sussex (BA 1969–1972) and the University of Oxford (DPhil 1972–1978), later serving as Bowra Research Fellow at Wadham College and professor at the University of Bristol (1980–2011).

Paul de Lagarde was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at Berlin and Halle-Wittenberg, including under Friedrich Rückert, and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1851–1854) and the University of Göttingen (1869–1891).

Paula Kane Robinson Arai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Waseda, Kalamazoo College, and Harvard (PhD 1993), she held posts at Vanderbilt, LSU, and became Professor of Women and Buddhist Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2023.

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Collegio San Pancrazio (~1774–1776) and served at the Malabar Mission (1776–1789), the Congregation of the Index (1800), and the Pontifical Urban University (1800).

Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, he served at the University of Rangoon as Professor of Pali (1912) and Principal (1937–1946), later heading the University of Adult Education and Burma Historical Commission.
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez studied Buddhist studies at the University of Sunderland, earning an MA under the instruction of Peter Harvey.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed a BA at National Taiwan University and a PhD (2002) at UCLA under Donald F. McCallum, also studying under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

Pema Bhum specializes in Tibetology. He formerly served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and was Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön works in Buddhist studies. Educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley, she studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Dzigar Kongtrul, and others, later serving as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center (1979–1984) and abbess and director at Gampo Abbey.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab and Khenpo Shenga.
Pema Tsering, a scholar in Tibetology, studied under Khenpo Shenga and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga, and taught Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Khenpo Shenga.
Penghao Sun is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under Leonard van der Kuijp, Qingying Chen, Weirong Shen, and others.
Penor 02 both studied under and taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Dilgo Khyentse, Jampel Gyepai Dorje, and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

Pentti Aalto worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki under Gustaf John Ramstedt (~1934–1950) and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics from 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen (1971–1990) and held posts at Copenhagen (1982–1989), the University of Bonn (1991–1992), and the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).
